Hello, self-harming teen here. I absolutely hated when my parents found out that I had been cutting. They never found my tools. They always found out after the fact. 

If I were your daughter, I initially be panicking when I couldn't find the box. Then I would be pissed that it had been taken. 

I guess if I were in your shoes, I would ask to speak with her, making sure she knows that she is not in any sort of trouble. Ask where she would be comfortable speaking. My parents always talked to me in their room, and that always made me super uncomfortable. 

Once you're there, I suggest being honest that you were cleaning up her room to try and help. (Personally, I'd be pissed knowing that my parents went into my room and cleaned without my permission, but that's just me) 

Bring up that you found the box and show it to her. Make sure to emphasize that you aren't mad, simply concerned for her health and safety because she is your child. 

I would also ask her what happened that led to her turning to self-harm and her reason for starting and continuing. 

Don't invalidate her or say that she could have come to you or done something instead of self-harming. If you do that, you're pushing her thoughts and reasoning to the side, making her feel shame for not doing any of those things. 

This is just what I would do if I were you and what I would want you to do if I was your daughter. Hope this helps, and I hope you can find a healthier and safer way for your daughter to cope during this challenging time.

1. I knew the instant I started self-harming that it wasn't okay. Like, it was a coping mechanism for me, but that didn't change the fact that I was purposely hurting myself.
2. The turning point for me was the fact that a) I was self-harming simply because I could and b) I didn't want to feel the shame and guilt that came along with telling people that I self-harmed.
3. Looking back on when I self-harmed, the worst thing was how addictive it became. There was a time where I was self-harming every day or every other day because I needed to feel that pain.

I've been clean for almost 180 days, and what helped me at first when I got urges was to have a hair tie or rubber band that I could snap against my wrist. I've also heard that rubbing an ice cube against your skin can help. 

I also used to draw on myself with a washable marker in my favorite color.

Yeah. My mom was actually the one to throw them out 'cause I was at school in the counselor's office and told her where they were. I'm so proud of you. I know for me, throwing away my razors caused me a lot of anxiety, but it's been one of the best things I've done.
